1vlhwtfrmsu: A suppression rule hides alerts **that are not relevant** to the organization. You can create one for one or more alert types, or from an existing alert (Take action, Suppress similar alerts, Create suppression rule). Scope: subscriptions through the portal or the REST API; management groups through **Azure Policy**. A rule applies only to alert types **already triggered at least once**. The elements to define: subscriptions, alert types (Custom or All), **entity conditions** to limit it to specific resources or values, name (2 to 50 characters, letters, digits, hyphens and underscores), enabled or disabled state, reason, comment, **expiration** (custom date or none) and the **Simulate** option to test the rule before applying it. Deleting a rule does not change the status of the alerts it has already closed.
tr54c28m52: An overly broad suppression is a permanent blind spot. Good practice rules: never “All” without a documented exception; always **entity conditions**; default **expiration** (for example 90 days) and review before renewal; **simulation** before application; approval by the risk owner; a register of rules with reason, author and date; and a quarterly review that compares active rules with the alerts avoided. A suppression does not fix the cause: if an alert comes back every week, first look for the configuration or process that produces it.
